nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The alarm says 6:40. The light under the door says the street is already awake. I have been a salary man for nine years, and I have never once wanted to get up.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The kettle takes four minutes. I count them. The 8:12 is the only train that leaves before the platform gets crowded, and it is the only train I can still board without running. Shoes. Bag. The key ring has three keys and one that opens nothing. I have carried it for years. I am not going to be the night I put it down.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The kettle is on. The bag is by the door. There is a second key on the ring, the one that opens nothing, and I have carried it for years. What do I do with it.

choices.text: Put it in the bag. Carry it. Nine more years of carrying.
Leave it on the table. Let it stay.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The door closes. The building exhales. Somewhere below, the convenience store light is already on. It is on at 2 AM. It is on at 6 AM. It is always on, and I have never once wondered why.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: You look like you slept in a filing cabinet.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I slept six hours. That is more than most nights this week.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Onesot. Two eggs. You're going to run out of steam by lunch and then you'll be that guy who stares at the vending machine like it owes him money.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The vending machine is honest. It takes my money and gives me exactly what I paid for. I have learned to value that in things.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Hey. You okay? You've been doing this 'honest vending machine' thing for a week. People don't do that unless something's wrong.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Something is wrong. I don't know what. I know the 8:12 is leaving in eleven minutes and I know I have to walk faster to make it.

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Walk fast. But if you're going to stand at the end of the platform and not get on, I want you to tell me first. That's not a rule. That's me.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I'll tell you. The platform is the next thing. The rest is the train, or the rest is nothing.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The platform is half full. Everyone is doing the thing where they stand very still and look at their phones, and the train comes, and the thing is over, and tomorrow the thing starts again.

nodes.speaker: Daichi
nodes.text: Oh, it's you. Sorry, sorry, I was in the middle of a thing. You know what I mean. A thing. The thing that's happening to everyone right now.

nodes.speaker: Daichi
nodes.text: Three projects. Three. My manager says 'synergy' like it's a word. I have a meeting about the meeting at four. Did you eat? You look like you didn't eat. I didn't eat. We're the same.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I had a onesot. Two eggs.

nodes.speaker: Daichi
nodes.text: Two eggs. Respect. I'm on a coffee-and-regret diet. Listen, you're not getting on today, are you. You have that look. The look. I had the look last month. I got on anyway. I regret it daily.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The 8:12 is pulling in. I can see it from here. The doors are going to open in about ninety seconds, and I have to decide what I do with the next nine years of my life in the next ninety seconds.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Daichi is beside me. He is looking at me. He is not talking, which is the first time I have seen him not talking. 'You want it, you want it,' he says. 'I'm just going to be here.' The doors are opening. What do I do.

choices.text: Step on. The 8:12. Nine more years.
Step off. Not today. Not this one.
Wait. Let this one go. Take the next.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I step on. The doors close behind me with a sound like a small, final decision. The train lurches. Daichi is in the next car, or the one after that, or maybe he's on a different line entirely. I don't follow.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I find a window. The platform slides back. The city slides back. The 8:12 does what it has always done, which is carry me to a building where I will sit in a chair and do a thing, and then another thing, and then the train home, and then the alarm, and then the 8:12.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Mina's voice is still in my ear. 'If you're going to stand at the end of the platform and not get on, I want you to tell me first.' I didn't stand at the end of the platform. I got on. I don't know what that means. I'll find out by lunch, maybe.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The train goes under the river at 8:14. I watch the water go dark. I have done this four thousand times. I am still not used to it. I think I will never be used to it. That is the whole point, maybe. That you are never used to it.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: At the office, the chair is the same chair. The light is the same light. The thing is the same thing. I sit down. I open the laptop. The screen says 'Good morning, Kenji.' I have never once wanted it to say anything else.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The 8:12 took me to work. Tomorrow the 8:12 will take me to work again. The convenience store light will be on at 2 AM. I will not wonder why. That is the commute. That is what it is. That is what it has always been.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I step off. Not off the train. Off the thing. The doors are still open and I am still on the platform and the train is still here and I am still here and I have decided, in ninety seconds, to not get on.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The doors close. The train pulls away. Daichi looks at me with an expression I can't read, which is the most honest look anyone has given me in years. 'You did it,' he says. 'You actually did it.' I don't answer. I don't know what to say.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I walk to the stairs. I walk up the stairs. I stand in the street and the street is loud and the street is awake and the street does not care what I have decided, which is the most kind thing anyone has done for me all day.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I pull out my phone. Mina. 'I'm not getting on.' Three words. I stare at them for a long time. Then I send them. The phone buzzes back before I've put it away.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The phone is in my hand. The street is loud. Mina is going to come find me, and I have to tell her where. What do I say.

choices.text: 'I'm at the stairs. The ones by the platform. I'm not moving.'
'I'm at the shop. The one with the light. I'll be there in ten.'

nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.text: Okay. Where are you. I'm coming. Don't move. Don't get on anything. Don't be brave. Just be where you are and let me come find you.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I stand in the street. The sun is doing the thing where it comes up and pretends it didn't. I am not brave. I am not going to be brave. I am just here, in the street, in the morning, in the first minute of a day that is not the 8:12. That is enough. That has to be enough.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: I wait. The doors open. I don't get on. The doors close. The train goes. I stand on the platform and I watch it go and I feel something I can't name, which is not relief and not fear and not either of those things.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Daichi is beside me. He is not talking. This is the first time I have seen him not talking. He looks at the train go. He looks at me. 'The next one's in four minutes,' he says. 'You want it, you want it. I'm not going to stop you. I'm not going to encourage you either. I'm just going to be here.'

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Four minutes. I count them. The platform fills with the next wave of people, the 8:16 crowd, the ones who missed the 8:12 and are now doing the standing-very-still thing with their phones. I am not doing that thing. I am standing here, waiting, and the waiting is the point.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Mina's message comes through. 'You didn't get on. Good. The next one, or the one after that, or none of them. I'm not mad. I'm just here. I'll be at the shop. The onesot's on me. Don't be late.' I almost smile. Almost.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: The 8:16 pulls in. I watch it. I do not get on. I walk to the stairs. I walk up the stairs. I walk to the shop. The light is on. It is always on. I walk in. Mina is behind the counter, and she is smiling, and she does not say 'you did it,' she just says 'onesot or two eggs,' and I say 'two eggs,' and the day is not the 8:12, and the day is not over, and the day is, for the first time in nine years, mine.

THE COMMUTE. The 8:12 took him to work. It will take him to work again tomorrow, and the day after that, and the day after that. The convenience store light will be on at 2 AM. He will not wonder why. That is the commute. That is what it is. That is what it has always been. That is what it will be.

THE STEP OFF. He stood in the street in the first minute of a day that was not the 8:12. He was not brave. He was not going to be brave. He was just here, in the street, in the morning, and Mina was coming to find him, and the day was not over, and the day was, for the first time in nine years, not the 8:12. That was enough. That had to be enough.

THE DELAY. He let the 8:12 go. He watched it go. He walked to the shop. The light was on. It was always on. Mina was behind the counter, and she was smiling, and she did not say 'you did it,' she just said 'onesot or two eggs,' and he said 'two eggs,' and the day was not the 8:12, and the day was not over, and the day was, for the first time in nine years, his. Not the 8:12's. His.
